data.title: Livsayis™ (cemdisiran) Approved by the FDA as First and Only siRNA Therapy in Generalized Myasthenia Gravis and Only Treatment with Four-Times-a-Year Subcutaneous Dosing
data.description:
Approval based on Phase 3 NIMBLE results demonstrating rapid, deep and sustained disease control that is maintained throughout three-month dosing intervals

Livsayis is Regeneron's first approved siRNA therapy and neurology medicine

TARRYTOWN, N.Y., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Livsayis™ (cemdisiran) for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult patients who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive, the predominant form of the disease. Livsayis is a novel, complement component factor 5 (C5)-directed small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutic that reduces levels of circulating C5 protein, limiting terminal complement activation, a key driver of the disease. It is the first and only approved siRNA therapy in gMG and the only FDA-approved gMG treatment administered subcutaneously four times a year.

“For people living with gMG, every day can be unpredictable, due to fluctuating muscle weakness and fatigue. They may also experience severe exacerbations that can be life-threatening. Many still experience suboptimal disease control, whether from waning of therapeutic effect, inadequate response or high treatment burden,” said Tuan Vu, M.D., Professor of Neurology at the University of South Florida Morsani College of Medicine, Division Director for Neuromuscular Medicine and EMG Laboratories, and a global principal investigator of the NIMBLE trial. “In the Phase 3 NIMBLE trial, Livsayis delivered rapid, deep disease control – maintained through the end of dosing intervals – and offers a four-times-a-year subcutaneous dosing schedule. These results highlight how a first-of-its-kind approach can address a key driver of disease and provide a compelling treatment option.”

The FDA approval was based on results from the Phase 3 NIMBLE trial. Livsayis demonstrated the following least square mean change from baseline:

  • 4.5-point improvement on the Myasthenia Gravis-Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) total score at 24 weeks (0.4 standard error [SE]) compared to a 2.2-point improvement with placebo (0.5 SE). This corresponded to a placebo-adjusted improvement of 2.3 points (p=0.0005). MG-ADL is a clinician-administered patient-reported assessment of daily functions impacted by gMG, such as talking, chewing, swallowing, breathing, vision and mobility. The proportion of MG-ADL responders with at least 3-point improvement at week 24 was greater for Livsayis (76.6%) compared to placebo (44.1%, p<0.001).
  • 4.2-point improvement in Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) total score at 24 weeks (0.6 SE) compared to a 1.5-point improvement with placebo (0.7 SE), corresponding to a placebo-adjusted improvement of 2.8 points (p=0.0015). QMG is a clinician-administered assessment of muscle function, including vision, speaking/swallowing, breathing and limb mobility. The proportion of QMG responders with at least a 5-point improvement at week 24 was greater for Livsayis (48.4%) compared to placebo (19.0%, p<0.001).
  • Rapid onset of clinically meaningful benefit in MG-ADL (2.5 points), with improvements seen as early as two weeks of starting treatment that deepened over time.
  • Sustained disease control and symptom relief through 24 weeks, with MG-ADL scores maintained and no indication of waning efficacy.

The prescribing information for Livsayis includes a Boxed Warning for serious meningococcal infections in addition to warnings and precautions for other serious infections, consistent with other FDA-approved medicines that reduce C5 activity. The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) in patients treated with Livsayis and more frequently than placebo were injection site reactions, viral infections and urinary tract infections. Livsayis is available only through a restricted program called the Livsayis Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS), which is also consistent with other FDA-approved medicines that reduce C5 activity. Details of the Important Safety Information are included below.

“Livsayis is Regeneron’s first approved medicine in neurology, and an important new option for people living with generalized myasthenia gravis who need effective disease control without a heavy treatment burden,” said George D. Yancopoulos, M.D., Ph.D., Board Co-Chair, President and Chief Scientific Officer of Regeneron. “As Regeneron’s first approved siRNA therapy, this approval marks a meaningful step forward for our neuroscience pipeline as we relentlessly pursue bold, new approaches to transform care for people living with serious neurological diseases.”

“Individuals living with gMG experience profound muscle weakness that can affect how they talk, see, breathe and move, and with it their ability to carry out everyday activities,” said Samantha Masterson, President & CEO, Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America. “This approval is a positive milestone for the gMG community, reflecting continued progress on outcomes that matter most to patients. With Livsayis, those living with generalized myasthenia gravis have a new option that may help maintain disease control while reducing the burden treatment can place on daily life.”

Regeneron is committed to supporting people living with rare diseases and ensuring patients who have been prescribed Livsayis access to their medication. Regeneron’s myRARE™ program offers resources to help patients and healthcare providers, including product information, insurance benefit verification, and information about potential financial support. To learn about myRARE, visit myRARE.com or call 1-833-4my-RARE (1-833-469-7273).

A regulatory submission for Livsayis for the treatment of gMG is currently under review in the European Union, with a decision anticipated in the second half of 2027. Regulatory submissions are planned in additional markets, including Japan.

About gMG

gMG is a rare, chronic autoimmune disease characterized by unpredictable, debilitating and potentially life-threatening muscle weakness. In the most common form of the disease, abnormal anti-AChR antibodies activate the complement system including C5, disrupting communication between nerves and muscles, which contributes to damage at the neuromuscular junction. For these patients, the disease affects muscles throughout the body, resulting in extreme fatigue and difficulties with facial expression, speech, swallowing, mobility, breathing as well as severe exacerbations, including myasthenic crisis that can impair breathing to the point of requiring hospitalization. Worldwide, an estimated 150 to 200 out of every million people have MG. In the U.S., the disease impacts approximately 85,000 people.

About Livsayis

Livsayis is the first approved siRNA therapy for gMG and the only gMG treatment FDA-approved to be administered subcutaneously four times per year (every three months).

Livsayis is a complement C5-directed siRNA that degrades the messenger RNA (mRNA) that encodes the C5 protein, thereby blocking C5 production, reducing circulating levels of C5 and inhibiting terminal complement activation, a key driver of AChR-positive gMG.

Regeneron is solely responsible for the development, manufacturing, and commercialization of Livsayis through a worldwide licensing agreement with Alnylam.

About the NIMBLE trial

NIMBLE is the largest global, interventional gMG trial conducted to date. In this ongoing Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, Livsayis is being evaluated in patients with anti-AChR antibody-positive gMG who can continue background immunosuppressants based on the investigator’s discretion. Participants were randomized to receive one of four subcutaneous regimens: Livsayis every three months; a combination of Livsayis and a C5-inhibiting monoclonal antibody every 4 weeks; C5-inhibiting monoclonal antibody every 4 weeks; or placebo every 4 weeks.

The primary endpoint assessed changes in the MG-ADL total score from baseline to week 24. The MG-ADL scale is an eight-question clinician-administered, patient-reported tool that measures how gMG affects aspects of daily life and provides a total score ranging from 0 to 24. The key secondary endpoint was the change from baseline in QMG total score at week 24. The QMG is a clinician-administered 13-item standardized assessment evaluating muscle function that provides a total score ranging from 0 to 39. In both MG-ADL and QMG, a higher total score indicates greater disease severity, and a larger reduction in total score indicates greater improvement in disease symptoms and better treatment effect.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

What is the most important information I should know about LIVSAYIS?

LIVSAYIS is a medicine that affects part of your immune system. LIVSAYIS may lower the ability of your immune system to fight certain infections.

  • LIVSAYIS increases your chance of getting serious meningococcal infections caused by Neisseria meningitidis bacteria. Meningococcal infections may quickly become life-threatening or cause death if not recognized and treated early.
    • You must complete your meningococcal vaccines at least 2 weeks before your first dose of LIVSAYIS.
    • If you have not completed your meningococcal vaccines, and LIVSAYIS must be started right away, you should receive the required vaccines as soon as possible.
    • If you have not been vaccinated and LIVSAYIS must be started right away, you must also receive antibiotics.
    • If you had a meningococcal vaccine in the past, you might need additional vaccination before starting LIVSAYIS. Your healthcare provider will decide if you need additional meningococcal vaccination.
    • Meningococcal vaccines do not prevent all meningococcal infections. Call your healthcare provider or get emergency medical help right away if you get any of these signs and symptoms of a meningococcal infection: fever, fever and a rash, fever with high heart rate, headache with nausea or vomiting, headache and a fever, headache with a stiff neck or stiff back, confusion, muscle aches with flu-like symptoms, or eyes sensitive to light

Your healthcare provider will give you a Patient Safety Card about the risk of serious meningococcal infection. Carry it with you at all times during treatment and for 12 months after your last LIVSAYIS dose. Your risk of meningococcal infection may continue for several months after your last dose of LIVSAYIS. It is important to show this card to any healthcare provider who treats you. This will help them diagnose and treat you quickly.

LIVSAYIS is only available through a program called the LIVSAYIS Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS). Before you can receive LIVSAYIS, your healthcare provider must: enroll in the LIVSAYIS REMS program; counsel you about the risk of serious meningococcal infections; give you the Patient Guide that explains your risk of serious meningococcal infections; give you a Patient Safety Card that has important information about the signs and symptoms of meningococcal infections; make sure that you are vaccinated against serious infections caused by meningococcal bacteria, and that you receive antibiotics if you need to start LIVSAYIS right away and you are not up-to-date on your vaccines.

LIVSAYIS may also increase the risk of other types of serious infections especially those caused by encapsulated bacteria, including Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Certain people may be at risk of serious infections with gonorrhea. Talk to your healthcare provider about whether you are at risk for gonorrhea infection, about gonorrhea prevention, and regular testing.

Call your healthcare provider right away if you have new signs or symptoms of infection.

Who should not receive LIVSAYIS?

  • Do not receive LIVSAYIS if you have a serious meningococcal infection when you are starting LIVSAYIS treatment.

Before you receive LIVSAYIS, tell your healthcare provider about all your medical conditions, including if you:

  • Have an infection or fever
  • Are pregnant or plan to be pregnant. It is not known whether LIVSAYIS will harm your unborn baby
  • Are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed. It is not known if LIVSAYIS passes into your breast milk

Tell your healthcare provider about medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements. Know the medicines you take and the vaccines you receive. Keep a list of them to show your healthcare provider and pharmacist when you get a new medicine.

The most common side effects in people with gMG treated with LIVSAYIS include: injection site reactions, viral infections and urinary tract infections.

Tell your healthcare provider about any side effect that bothers you or that does not go away. These are not all the possible side effects of LIVSAYIS. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Please see full Prescribing Information, including Boxed WARNING, and Medication Guide for LIVSAYIS.

What is LIVSAYIS?

LIVSAYIS is a prescription medicine used to treat a disease called generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adults who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody positive.

It is not known if LIVSAYIS is safe and effective in children.

About Regeneron

Regeneron is a leading biotechnology company that invents, develops and commercializes life-transforming medicines for people with serious diseases. Founded and led by physician-scientists, our unique ability to repeatedly and consistently translate science into medicine has led to numerous approved treatments and product candidates in development, most of which were homegrown in our laboratories. Our medicines and pipeline are designed to help patients with eye diseases, allergic and inflammatory diseases, cancer, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, neurological diseases, hematologic conditions, infectious diseases, and rare diseases.

Regeneron pushes the boundaries of scientific discovery and accelerates drug development using our proprietary technologies, such as VelociSuite®, which produces optimized fully human antibodies and new classes of bispecific antibodies. We are shaping the next frontier of medicine with data-powered insights from the Regeneron Genetics Center® and pioneering genetic medicine platforms, enabling us to identify innovative targets and complementary approaches to potentially treat or cure diseases.

For more information, please visit www.Regeneron.com or follow Regeneron on LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook or X.

data.title: Sanford Bull Sees Strong Cash Generation in FY27 — Market Talk
data.description: Sanford's bull at Forsyth Barr shrugs off the prospect of lower profitability in FY27. That's because the New Zealand company had an exceptional squid season a year earlier, which will make it hard for FY27 wildcatch earnings to beat FY26. Analyst Paul Laxton Koraua also points to an unwinding of salmon biomass valuation gains in FY27 and further pressure on Sanford's mussels division. "However, cash generation should remain strong, supporting our forecast for a broadly net cash position by the end of FY27," Forsyth Barr says. It retains an "outperform" call on Sanford, noting its one-year forward price-to-earnings multiple of 11x represents an around 34% discount to the market median. Sanford is unchanged, at NZ$7.00, today. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)

data.title: UniCredit and Germany reach broad agreement on Commerzbank takeover
data.description:
By Holger Hansen

UniCredit and Germany have reached agreement on the big sticking points in the Italian bank's takeover of Commerzbank, a major development in the two-year battle for control of the German lender.

The agreement, laid out in a letter from UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel to German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil as well as a separate statement to Reuters from the German minister, states that the merged bank's German headquarters will remain in Frankfurt as a listed entity, a key German demand.

But Germany has given up its insistence on naming two supervisory board members to Commerzbank , in a concession to UniCredit.

A combination of UniCredit and Commerzbank would create a bank with more than €1.3 trillion ($1.43 trillion) in assets across two of the euro zone's ​largest economies in one of the most significant cross-border European banking deals in years.

In the letter dated November 18 and seen by Reuters, Orcel said he was "prepared to commit" to a series of binding principles and thanked Klingbeil for discussions "which have allowed us to find common ground."

UniCredit also pledged to put German nationals on UniCredit's board of directors.

Klingbeil, in his statement to Reuters, said Germany "supports a swift process and an orderly transition of control."

"We have reached common ground and UniCredit has made clear commitments to Germany as a business location, to the rights of Commerzbank employees and to a continued constructive dialogue with the works council in the further process," Klingbeil said, referring to a body of elected employee representatives.

Orcel pounced on Commerzbank in 2024, taking the lender and the government off guard by discreetly building up a holding. Commerzbank and Berlin tried to prevent the ⁠takeover, ​but gave in after UniCredit amassed a stake nearing ​50%.

The German government holds a 13.3% stake in Commerzbank following a bailout during the global financial crisis.

($1 = 0.9115 euros)

data.title: Hy-Vee Health with Oscar Expands Across Iowa, Into Kansas City and Omaha for 2027 Open Enrollment
data.description:
Hy-Vee, Inc. ("Hy-Vee"), a leading grocery store in the Midwest, and Oscar, one of the fastest-growing insurers in the individual market and part of Oscar Health (), today announced that Hy-Vee Health with Oscar is expanding statewide across Iowa and launching in Kansas City and Omaha for 2027 Open Enrollment.1

Beginning Nov. 1, 2026, individuals and families can enroll in Hy-Vee Health with Oscar directly through HealthCare.gov for 2027 coverage. Employees in CHOICE Arrangements (formerly ICHRA) can also enroll using their tax-free monthly employer contributions.

Hy-Vee became joint owner of Exemplar Care in 2024, rebranding the direct primary care practice as Hy-Vee Health Exemplar Care and helping the practice expand to more than 17 clinic locations across the Midwest.

The Hy-Vee Health with Oscar plan makes getting care as easy as shopping at Hy-Vee. Members get a full suite of healthcare, lifestyle, and shopping benefits in one comprehensive package:

  • Budget-friendly coverage and medications: Competitive monthly premiums and affordable prescriptions available at Hy-Vee pharmacies for individuals and the whole family.

  • Free care at Hy-Vee Health Exemplar Care2 (a $2,600 value for a family of four3): $0 primary care, urgent care, and telehealth visits; $0 annual and routine labs; and $0 on 100-plus generic medications.

  • More doctors and hospitals: Iowa members have exclusive access to University of Iowa Health Care, MercyOne, and UnityPoint health systems. Members in Kansas City have access to HCA Midwest Health, University of Kansas Health System, and AdventHealth System. Omaha members receive access to CHI Health and Nebraska Methodist Health System.

  • One-on-one guidance: Every member gets access to dedicated Oscar Care Guides and an everyday AI health guide, Oswell4, to help members find care, understand benefits, and receive personalized guidance.

  • Everyday rewards: $50 in Hy-Vee rewards redeemable on groceries, gas, dietitian services, and more.

"Hy-Vee Health with Oscar makes offering competitive benefits easy and affordable for businesses of all sizes,” explained Geoff Bartsh, Senior Vice President of Markets for Oscar Insurance. “As we grow across the Midwest, we’re excited to make healthcare simple, accessible, and affordable for more communities, paired with everyday savings from Hy-Vee.”

“We are proud to expand our partnership with Oscar to bring affordable, high-quality care to more Midwest families through the providers, pharmacies, and stores they know and trust,” said Dr. Jon Van Der Veer, Founder and CEO of Hy-Vee Health Exemplar Care.

Employers can enroll their teams at hioscar.com/for-employers, or through their broker. Individuals, families, and employees can sign up through Jan, 15, 2027:

  • Iowa: Visit HealthCare.gov, call 1-833-419-8482, or connect with an insurance agent. Employees receiving tax-free contributions from work, should check with their employers for details.

  • Johnson County, Kansas, and Jackson County, Missouri (Kansas City metro): Visit hioscar.com/get-coverage or connect with an insurance agent.

  • Douglas County, Nebraska (Omaha metro): Visit hioscar.com/get-coverage or connect with an insurance agent.

Oscar Insurance is one of the largest and fastest-growing health insurers dedicated to the individual market. Oscar serves millions of individuals across the country with innovative products and CHOICE Arrangement solutions (formerly ICHRA) tailored to their life stages, health needs, and budgets. Oscar technology-powered experiences make high-quality care easy to use and feel personal. Oscar is part of Oscar Health, Inc. (). Learn more at HiOscar.com.

About Hy-Vee Health Exemplar Care
Hy-Vee Health Exemplar Care is a membership-based healthcare organization addressing the evolving needs of today’s patients through accessible, transparent, and relationship-driven care. Operating clinics across five Midwest states, Hy-Vee Health Exemplar Care offers healthcare through flexible membership options designed to meet patients where they are in their health journey. The organization is focused on strengthening patient-provider relationships and delivering a more trusted, sustainable healthcare experience.

data.title: Agereh Technologies Inc. Closes First Tranche of Private Placement
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Agereh Technologies Inc. ("Agereh" or the "Company") is pleased to announce it has closed the first tranche (the "First Tranche") of its previously announced non-brokered private placement (the "Offering"). As previously announced on October 16, 2026, the Offering consists of up to 24,000,000 units of the Company ("Units") at a price of $0.025 per Unit for gross proceeds of up to $600,000. The First Tranche consisted of 7,600,000 Units issued at a price of $0.025 per Unit for aggregate gross proceeds of $190,000.00.

Each Unit under the Offering consists of one (1) common share of the Company (each, a "Share") and one (1) common share Purchase Warrant (each, a "Warrant"), with each Warrant entitling the holder to purchase one (1) additional Share at a price of $0.05 per Share for a period of two (2) years from the date of issue.

The Company intends to use the net proceeds of the First Tranche to support: (i) ongoing product development activities, including research and development and technology enhancement; (ii) sales and marketing activities, including business development efforts, customer outreach initiatives, and attendance at industry conferences and trade shows; and (iii) general working capital purposes, including accounting, legal, regulatory compliance, and other administrative expenses. Management fees, if incurred, are expected to represent only a minor portion of the net proceeds. The Company did not pay any bonus, finder's fee, commission, Agent's options or other compensation to any third party in connection with the closing of this First Tranche.

No related parties or the Company, as such term is defined Multilateral Instrument 61-101 - Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101") participated in the First Tranche, and no non-arm's length parties of the Company acquired securities under the First Tranche.

All securities issued under the Offering, including securities issuable on the exercise thereof, will be subject to a hold period expiring four (4) months and one (1) day from the date of issuance, in accordance with applicable laws and the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange.

The Offering remains subject to the acceptance of the TSX Venture Exchange. The Company expects to close the remaining tranche(s) of the Offering by November 30, 2026.

About Agereh Technologies Inc.

Agereh Technologies Inc. is a Canadian-based artificial intelligence and advanced technology company delivering AI-enabled platforms and sensor solutions to address critical challenges in the transportation industry. data.title: UGI Corporation Announces Plan to Pursue the Separation of Its Global Liquefied Petroleum Gas Business Into a Standalone Public Company
data.description:
UGI Corporation () today announced that its Board of Directors unanimously approved a plan to pursue the separation of its Global LPG business (the new LPG Company) from UGI to create two publicly traded companies, each well-capitalized with tailored capital allocation strategies and strongly positioned to serve customers, pursue strategic growth objectives and create significant, long-term shareholder value. UGI intends to execute the separation through a spinoff of the new LPG Company that is expected to be tax-free to UGI and its shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes. The spinoff is expected to be completed during the second half of calendar year 2027.

“The creation of the new LPG Company is the next step in our company’s transformation, building on the portfolio optimization, balance sheet strengthening, and operational improvements we have achieved. The separation positions both companies for long-term growth, strategic optionality, and significant value creation for shareholders and customers,” said President and Chief Executive Officer, Robert Flexon. “Each company will have distinct strategies and operating priorities with capital allocation and supporting resources directed to its greatest opportunities for success and market leadership.”

Flexon continued, “We move forward with great confidence in the future of both companies and their respective abilities to serve customers and communities with excellence.”

Anticipated Benefits of the Planned Separation

As separate companies, the New UGI and the new LPG Company are expected to benefit from:

  • Sharper strategic alignment: Focused management and business models aligned with each company’s markets, customers, and capital needs;

  • Tailored capital structures: Balance sheets and capital return policies aligned to each company’s financial profile and cost of capital;

  • Capital and strategic flexibility: Investments aligned with each company’s growth opportunities and other long-term shareholder value-creating alternatives; and

  • Distinct investment profiles: Discrete business models allowing investors to assess each company based on its operational and financial characteristics.

New UGI: A Premier Natural Gas Infrastructure Company in the Mid-Atlantic Region

Following the completion of the separation, the New UGI will be a premier natural gas infrastructure company with fully regulated natural gas utilities and complementary midstream assets located in a favorable long-term supply basin, with direct access to low-cost Marcellus and Utica supply, and ideally positioned to serve customers demanding safe, reliable, and affordable natural gas in the Mid-Atlantic region. Demand megatrends for natural gas, including the need for generation to support the power grid, data center development, and rising industrial activity, are expected to further drive sustainable growth for the New UGI. Its operations will include:

  • UGI Utilities, Inc.: Operates the second largest regulated natural gas utility in Pennsylvania, serving approximately 700,000 customers across 46 counties;

  • Mountaineer Gas Company: The largest regulated natural gas utility in West Virginia, serving more than 209,000 customers across 55 counties; and

  • UGI Energy Services, LLC: Includes natural gas pipeline and gathering assets with a total capacity of 5.1 MMDth/day and storage facilities with approximately 15 Bcf of capacity, as well as LNG peaking assets.

The New UGI is expected to benefit from consistent earnings growth and solid, recurring cash flows backed by a constructive regulatory framework that allows over 90% recoverability of capital spend within 12 months, a $5 billion regulated rate base expected to grow 8 – 10% per year, and fee-based contract structures covering more than 80% of midstream margins. Approximately 90% of the New UGI’s margins are de-risked through its regulated utility operations, take-or-pay and minimum volume commitments, and fixed-fee arrangements. Cash flows for the New UGI are expected to be directed to capital investments that promote safe, reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy; targeted system expansion opportunities; maintaining a strong balance sheet and investment-grade credit profile; and an attractive dividend for shareholders.

As a regulated utility and in keeping with UGI’s current focus on affordability and service excellence, the separation transaction should not have an impact on customers or customer rates.

New LPG Company: The Largest Publicly Traded LPG Distribution Company in the World Following the Separation

The new standalone LPG Company is expected to be a scaled leader in Europe and the largest retail propane distributor in the United States. The new LPG Company’s assets meet critical energy needs in the regions it serves and are strategically located near diverse supply channels, providing a competitive advantage that has resulted in a broad and diverse customer base spanning the residential, commercial, industrial, and agricultural sectors. With resilient unit margins, a targeted EBITDA margin of 17 – 20%, and expected growth in free cash flow, the new LPG Company will be well positioned to deliver a compelling and growing dividend, combined with share repurchases, while investing in targeted growth opportunities. Its operations will include:

  • UGI International: A leading distributor of LPG in nine countries in western and northern Europe and the largest in France, Belgium, Denmark, Luxembourg and Finland; and

  • AmeriGas Propane, Inc.: Serves approximately 950,000 customers in 49 states from approximately 1,300 distribution locations and a network of more than 41,700 cylinder-exchange outlets.

Contract structures and hedging programs within the new LPG Company will continue to support strong cash flow generation. UGI International has a track record of solid operational execution, and AmeriGas Propane has made meaningful progress on its operating improvement and safety initiatives while strengthening its balance sheet, leaving the business better positioned for volumetric growth. Building on these efforts will be a priority for the new LPG Company as it enters its next phase of growth.

Following the separation, cash flows for the new LPG Company, are expected to be directed to a compelling and growing dividend, share repurchases, and targeted strategic growth investments, while maintaining a strong balance sheet and industry-leading credit profile.

Separation Transaction Details

Under the proposed spinoff plan, UGI’s shareholders will retain their current shares of UGI common stock and receive a pro-rata distribution of shares of the new LPG Company’s stock in a transaction that is intended to be tax-free to UGI and its shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes. After the completion of the spinoff, the New UGI may retain a stake of up to 19.9% in the new LPG Company, which would be exited in a tax-efficient manner over time.

The spinoff transaction is subject to final approval from the UGI Board of Directors, the effectiveness of a registration statement on Form 10 to be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, and satisfaction of other customary conditions, including receipt of required consents, waivers or amendments under our and our subsidiaries’ debt agreements, or repayment under or termination of such agreements. There can be no assurance that any separation transaction will ultimately occur or, if one does occur, its structure, terms, timing, or tax treatment.

UGI intends to continue its quarterly dividend, subject to approval by its Board of Directors, with a payout ratio in line with peers, building on its 142 consecutive years of dividend payments.

Further details regarding the proposed capital structure, capital allocation strategy, dividend policy, governance, and leadership team for each company will be defined as part of the separation planning and communicated at a later date.

Conference Call and Webcast

UGI will hold a live audio webcast of its conference call to discuss this announcement and its fiscal 2026 financial results at 8:00 AM ET on Thursday, November 19, 2026.

Interested parties may listen to the webcast both live and in replay on the Internet at https://www.ugicorp.com/investors/financial-reports/events-and-presentations or by visiting the UGI website at https://www.ugicorp.com and clicking on “Investors” and then “Events and Presentations.”

Advisors

J.P. Morgan Securities LLC is serving as lead financial advisor to UGI, and Latham & Watkins LLP is serving as legal advisor.

About UGI

UGI Corporation () is a distributor and marketer of energy products and services in the U.S. and Europe. UGI offers safe, reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy solutions to customers through its subsidiaries, which provide natural gas transmission and distribution, electric generation and distribution, midstream services, propane distribution, renewable natural gas generation, distribution and marketing, and energy marketing services.

Comprehensive information about UGI Corporation is available on the Internet at https://www.ugicorp.com.

Use of Non-GAAP Measures

Management uses free cash flow (“FCF”) and EBITDA margin, each a non-GAAP financial measure, to evaluate the new LPG Company’s cash generation and operating performance. Management believes these measures provide investors with useful supplemental information about the new LPG Company’s historical cash generation and expected performance, including its capacity to fund dividends, share repurchases and growth investments.

  • We define FCF as cash from operating activities and proceeds from the sale of assets in the normal course of business, less capital expenditures.

  • We define EBITDA margin as adjusted EBITDA divided by revenue.

These non-GAAP measures are not calculated in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”) and should be considered in addition to, and not as a substitute for, the most directly comparable GAAP measures.

Targets for EBITDA margin and expected growth in FCF are forward-looking non-GAAP measures. UGI has not provided reconciliations of these measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures because the information necessary for reconciliation to their most directly comparable GAAP measure is unavailable without unreasonable effort.

Use of Forward-Looking Statements

This press release contains statements, estimates and projections that are forward-looking statements (as defined in Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended). Such statements use forward-looking words such as “believe,” “plan,” “anticipate,” “continue,” “estimate,” “expect,” “intend,” “target,” “may,” or other similar words and terms of similar meaning, although not all forward-looking statements contain such words. These statements discuss plans, strategies, events or developments that we expect or anticipate will or may occur in the future. These include statements regarding the proposed separation of our LPG businesses into a separate publicly traded company; the timing, structure and completion of the separation, including its expected completion during the second half of calendar year 2027, and the proposed distribution of shares to UGI shareholders; the intended tax treatment of the transaction; the potential retention of a stake of up to 19.9% in the new LPG Company and subsequent exit from that stake, including the timing and intended tax treatment of such exit; the anticipated benefits of the separation, including enhanced strategic alignment and operating focus, investor recognition of each company’s value, tailored capital structures, financial policies and capital allocation strategies, increased capital and strategic flexibility to pursue growth opportunities and value-creating strategic options, distinct investment profiles, opportunities for employees and shareholder value creation; the expected composition, market positions, financial and operating performance, unit margins, cash flows, growth opportunities, rate base growth, capital investments and operating improvement, safety and deleveraging initiatives of the New UGI and the new LPG Company, including the new LPG Company’s targeted EBITDA margin and expected growth in free cash flow; the expected impact of the separation on customers and customer rates; capital structures, financial policies, dividend intentions, share repurchases, payout targets, credit-profile targets, governance and leadership for the companies, including UGI’s intended continuation of its quarterly dividend and targeted payout ratio pending completion of the separation; and the consideration of other pathways to maximize long-term shareholder value. Management believes that these are reasonable as of today’s date only. Actual results may differ significantly because of risks and uncertainties that are difficult to predict and many of which are beyond management’s control; accordingly, there is no assurance that results will be realized. Risks and uncertainties relating to the proposed separation and the companies’ businesses and expected performance include final approval by our Board of Directors; the effectiveness of the registration statement on Form 10; the satisfaction of other conditions necessary to complete the separation, including receipt of required consents, waivers or amendments under our and our subsidiaries’ debt agreements, or repayment under or termination of such agreements, on a timely basis or at all; the ability to qualify the separation for its intended tax treatment; the finalization of the companies’ capital structures and the completion of any necessary financing transactions on satisfactory terms; our ability to successfully separate the businesses, realize the anticipated benefits of the separation and achieve the expected market positions; the evaluation and pursuit of other strategic pathways that could affect the separation, its timing or its anticipated benefits; uncertainty regarding market conditions, investor perceptions and the trading prices of each company’s shares following the separation; the ability to exit any retained stake in the new LPG Company with the intended tax treatment; costs and disruptions caused by or related to the separation, including potential impacts on customers and customer rates; changes in energy demand, including whether anticipated natural gas demand from commercial and industrial activity, data center development and power generation materializes; regulatory outcomes and the ability to recover costs, earn expected returns on planned utility investments and achieve projected rate base growth; the availability and cost of natural gas and LPG supplies, weather conditions, commodity price fluctuations and the effectiveness of contract structures and hedging programs in supporting margins and cash flows; the ability of each company to generate sufficient cash flows to fund its planned capital allocation priorities and maintain its targeted credit profile, and the ability of the new LPG Company to achieve expected growth in free cash flow; board approval of dividends and share repurchases; and the ability of each company to manage and grow its businesses and execute its business and growth strategies following the separation, including operating improvement, safety and deleveraging initiatives. You should read UGI’s Annual Report on Form 10-K and Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q for a more extensive list of factors that could affect results. data.title: The stock market is being rocked by the biggest shake-up in a generation as tech falls behind
data.description:
By Joseph Adinolfi

Tech stocks are looking cheap, while defensive sectors like consumer staples are screening as expensive

The U.S. stock market has experienced a dramatic shake-up over the past couple of months.

Investors' sudden souring on the artificial-intelligence theme has coincided with a newfound fondness for shares of drugmakers and purveyors of consumer essentials like toothpaste and laundry detergent.

The shift has triggered one of the most dramatic stock-market shake-ups in decades. Not since the immediate aftermath of the dot-com bubble more than two decades ago have investors seen normally sleepy healthcare stocks outperform red-hot technology names by such a wide margin.

During the 100 days through Nov. 10, stocks in the S&P 500's healthcare sector XX:SP500.35 outperformed the index's information-technology names XX:SP500.45 by more than 33 percentage points, according to an analysis by Dow Jones Market Data.

That was the widest outperformance since October 2001. By then, the dot-com bubble had already burst, and major indexes were mired in a painful bear market made worse by the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks and a mild economic recession. As major indexes like the S&P 500 SPX and the Nasdaq Composite COMP struggled at the time, shares of Walmart (WMT) and other defensive stocks rallied.

As of Wednesday's close, healthcare was still outperforming tech by more than 22 percentage points - what would be its strongest relative performance since 2008, excluding earlier this year, Dow Jones Market Data showed.

Gina Martin Adams, chief market strategist at HB Wealth, framed the shift as merely a reversal of what investors had witnessed during the first half of 2026, when shares of semiconductor stocks and other "AI suppliers" zoomed higher at a pace that drew comparisons to the final leg of the dot-com bubble in late 1999.

"After what we saw in semiconductors in May and June, it makes sense that the reversal would be just as powerful," Martin Adams said during a conversation with MarketWatch.

The recent changing of the guard could be a buying opportunity for investors who regret not being more heavily exposed to the AI theme. Nicholas Colas, co-founder of DataTrek, wrote in commentary shared with MarketWatch that other recent extremes in the relationship between tech and healthcare stocks have been followed by sharp reversals.

Risk is cheap. Safety isn't.

Tech's recent troubles have turned another longstanding relationship in markets on its head.

Based on forward price-to-earnings ratio - a popular valuation metric used by Wall Street analysts - consumer staples XX:SP500.30 and healthcare are both trading at a premium to tech. This represents "a big divergence" from the dominant trend of the past decade, DataTrek's Colas pointed out.

Put another way, information-technology companies are extremely cheap relative to their expected earnings growth, while defensive staples are expensive. Other metrics tell a similar story.

Short-term momentum gauges like relative strength indexes show that tech stocks are oversold while staples are overbought, said Michael Lebowitz, a portfolio manager at RIA Advisors, during a conversation with MarketWatch.

"Risk is cheap, but safety is expensive," Lebowitz told MarketWatch on Wednesday.

As of earlier this week, the S&P 500 information-technology sector was trading at 16.9 times expected earnings over the next 12 months, its lowest forward price-to-earnings ratio since March 2020. Consumer staples were trading at nearly 25 times, while healthcare was at 19 times. This is also "a big divergence" from the dominant trend of the past decade, Colas noted.

The big question for investors right now is whether or not this rotation is just the latest to emerge since the start of this AI-driven bull market. Investors saw something similar in the summer of 2024, and again during the fourth quarter of 2025.

HB Wealth's Martin Adams said the latest market action was giving her a feeling of déjà vu, as investors were discussing many of the same themes and potential pitfalls late last year, when nontech stocks were having an earlier moment in the spotlight.

Lebowitz used the examples of Walmart and Nvidia (NVDA) to illustrate his point. Walmart is now trading at a forward price-to-earnings ratio above 45, while Nvidia's is around 16.

"Nvidia doesn't need much growth to be a better buy than Walmart here," Lebowitz said. "Unless there's a lot more to this whole Nvidia thing than meets the eye. That's the risk."

-Joseph Adinolfi

This content was created by MarketWatch, which is operated by Dow Jones & Co. MarketWatch is published independently from Dow Jones Newswires and The Wall Street Journal.
